source_date: 2023 (AASLD Practice Guidance on the Clinical Assessment and Management of NAFLD)

entries.title: When to suspect MASLD/NAFLD
entries.snippet: MASLD/NAFLD should be suspected in patients with hepatic steatosis on imaging or persistently elevated aminotransferases who have one or more cardiometabolic risk factors (overweight/obesity, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, atherogenic dyslipidemia) and absence of significant alcohol consumption or other competing etiologies. (Paraphrased.)
entries.source_org: American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases
entries.source_doc: AASLD Practice Guidance on the Clinical Assessment and Management of Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (2023)
entries.applies_when: adult with hepatic steatosis or persistent ALT/AST elevation and ≥1 metabolic risk factor
entries.demo_relevance: Kowalski: ALT 56, AST 48, hypertriglyceridemia, glucose 108 (prediabetes range), RUQ pain — high pretest probability for MASLD.

entries.title: FIB-4 as primary noninvasive risk stratifier
entries.snippet: FIB-4 is the recommended first-line noninvasive index for risk-stratifying patients with NAFLD/MASLD for advanced fibrosis. FIB-4 <1.3 indicates low risk and patients may be managed in primary care; FIB-4 1.3–2.67 (or >2.0 for age >65) indicates indeterminate/high risk warranting secondary assessment with VCTE (FibroScan) or ELF; FIB-4 >2.67 suggests high risk and hepatology referral. (Paraphrased.)
entries.source_org: American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases
entries.source_doc: AASLD Practice Guidance on the Clinical Assessment and Management of Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (2023)
entries.applies_when: adult with suspected MASLD; needs age, AST, ALT, and platelet count
entries.demo_relevance: Kowalski's labs (ALT/AST/age/plt) make FIB-4 directly computable as the first triage step.

entries.title: Quantify alcohol use; differentiate MASLD vs MetALD vs ALD
entries.snippet: Alcohol consumption should be carefully quantified using validated tools (e.g., AUDIT-C). Patients with cardiometabolic risk and steatosis are classified as MASLD when intake is below thresholds (<140 g/week women, <210 g/week men) and as MetALD at intermediate intake; greater intake suggests alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD). (Paraphrased.)
entries.source_org: American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases
entries.source_doc: AASLD Practice Guidance / 2023 Multisociety MASLD nomenclature
entries.applies_when: patient with steatosis and any reported alcohol use
entries.demo_relevance: Kowalski has documented alcohol use — alcohol quantification is required to classify MASLD vs MetALD vs ALD.

entries.title: Weight loss is the cornerstone intervention
entries.snippet: In adults with overweight or obesity and MASLD, weight loss achieved through hypocaloric diet and physical activity is recommended; ≥5% body-weight reduction reduces hepatic steatosis, ≥7–10% improves steatohepatitis and fibrosis. (Paraphrased.)
entries.source_org: American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases
entries.source_doc: AASLD Practice Guidance on the Clinical Assessment and Management of Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (2023)
entries.demo_relevance: Kowalski: lifestyle counseling is primary therapy; reinforce alongside alcohol reduction.

entries.title: Screen MASLD patients for T2DM and treat cardiovascular risk
entries.snippet: Patients with MASLD should be screened for type 2 diabetes (fasting glucose and/or HbA1c) and have cardiovascular risk factors aggressively managed, as ASCVD is the leading cause of death in this population. (Paraphrased.)
entries.source_org: American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases
entries.source_doc: AASLD Practice Guidance on the Clinical Assessment and Management of Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (2023)
entries.applies_when: adult with confirmed or suspected MASLD
entries.demo_relevance: Kowalski glucose 108 (impaired fasting glucose) — confirm with HbA1c; address lipids, BP.

entries.title: Abdominal ultrasound is the first-line imaging modality
entries.snippet: Conventional B-mode abdominal ultrasound is the recommended first-line imaging modality to detect hepatic steatosis in patients suspected of having MASLD. (Paraphrased.)
entries.source_org: American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases

entries.demo_relevance: Kowalski has RUQ pain + transaminitis — abdominal US is the first imaging step (also rules out gallbladder pathology).
